KEY MESSAGE 1...Widespread rain overspreads the region this evening 
and changes to a period of wet snow in the high terrain before 
tapering off early Fri. Any snow accumulations very minor with the 
greatest risk across the northern ORH Hills/Berks. Lingering rain 
Fri afternoon will mainly be across RI/SE MA and especially near the 
south coast. 

Outside of a few spot showers across southern New England this 
afternoon mainly across the interior...dry weather dominated. 
Despite a developing ESE low level jet...the model cross sections 
indicated a lot of low level dry air in the soundings which was 
resulting in mainly dry weather. However...as low pressure emerges 
off the mid-Atlantic coast a stronger LLJ/forcing will move into the 
region. As a result...we expect widespread rain to overspread the 
region this evening.

Thermal profiles do indicate that the atmosphere will become cold 
enough for a changeover to wet snow in the high terrain of the Berks 
and Worcester Hills overnight. The problem is that the overall 
duration/intensity of the wet snow looks to be limited. This a 
result of shortwave energy over southern Quebec which compresses the 
system to the south. You can see that by looking at the mid level 
centers/surface low pressure contours. It takes on more of an oval 
instead of spherical shape which indicates the storm being suppressed 
further south by northern stream shortwave energy. Therefore...the 
bulk of the precipitation will be ending early-mid morning Fri 
especially north of I-90. This should result in any snow 
accumulations being very minor across the high terrain of just a 
coating to perhaps an inch or two...generally at or above 1000 feet. 
Little if any travel impacts are expected other than perhaps brief 
slushy secondary roadways above 1000 feet with the greatest risk 
near 1500 feet along the east slopes of the Berks.

As we mentioned...the low pressure being suppressed to the south will 
result in the leftover rain Friday afternoon mainly confined to 
parts of RI/SE MA and especially near the south coast. There is a 
low risk that if the precipitation falls heavy enough a few brief 
snowflakes may even mix in for a time...but no accumulations/impacts 
expected. Otherwise...a raw chilly day with a gusty N wind and 
Fri afternoon temperatures mainly in the upper 30s to the lower 40s.

Otherwise...an abundance of clouds may linger Fri night given 
cyclonic flow but nothing more than a few spot showers across the 
far southeast New England coast. Otherwise...low temps should be 
held mainly in the 30s given lingering clouds and many places not 
decoupling. 

Lastly...gusty northerly winds coupled with astronomical high tides 
may result in splashover/very minor coastal flooding along north 
facing beaches across Cape Cod Bay and Nantucket sound. No 
significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor 
coastal flooding will be quite short-lived, no more than an hour on 
either side of high tide. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler, cloudy with northwest breezes this 
weekend. Mainly dry weather, but hit or miss scattered showers 
possible Saturday afternoon.

In the wake of the Friday storm system, we'll be left in a cool and 
moist cyclonic flow aloft as we move into the weekend. This will 
keep our weather pattern unsettled with more clouds than sun with 
northwesterly breezes. Amid the broader cyclonic flow aloft, models 
depict a pretty strong shortwave disturbance aloft rotating 
southward through New England Saturday afternoon into early evening. 
This will at least increase RH through the column with dynamic 
support associated with the shortwave could yield some scattered, 
hit-or-mostly-miss showers as the shortwave digs southward. Went 
ahead and added a mention of scattered showers for Saturday 
afternoon over the dry NBM, although limited to nil impacts with 
these showers. 

With the cool cyclonic flow (925 mb temps around 0 to -2C) and 
mostly cloudy/overcast conditions, highs on Saturday could end up 
rather chilly in the low to mid 40s lower elevations and upper 
30s/near 40 in the Berkshires and Worcester and Tolland hills. 
Slightly milder conditions in the mid/upper 40s lower elevations and 
low to mid 40s higher elevations for Sunday.  

KEY MESSAGE 3...Prolonged stretch of dry weather early to mid 
next week, with a warming trend to temperatures.

Strong multi-ensemble support for a modifying weather pattern as 500 
mb heights rise significantly, moving into early to midweek. This 
implies a steady warming trend to temperatures Monday through 
Wednesday (and potentially longer), but also supports several days 
of dry weather as surface ridging takes hold. Highs should rebound 
back into the upper 50s to mid 60s by Wed, which are about 5-10 
degrees above normal, and there is potential for those highs to be a 
couple degrees warmer as we get entrenched into the drier weather 
pattern.
